title: B.A. in Linguistics
description: Students are required to complete a minimum of 63 units of courses as follows:

sections.title: Faculty Package
text: LING1000# and any two courses from:

subsections.title: Research Components/ Capstone Courses/ Final Year Project

text: Six courses from the 3 Areas, with at least one course from each area, excluding LING3405 and 3406.

course_groups.label: Area 3: Language and Culture, and Linguistic Applications

subsections.title: Language courses to enhance students’ exposure to other language(s)
text: 6 units of language courses (from one to two languages) other than Chinese (Cantonese/Putonghua) and English, and excluding the 1-unit modern language courses, i.e. FREN1001, GERM1001, HKSL1001, KORE1001, and SPAN1001.

The tables show identifiable undergraduate language-learning options, not an exhaustive approved list. Choose courses in only one or two languages and check eligibility with the programme. Culture-only courses and 1-unit tasters are not included. Students whose first language is not Chinese should also see Explanatory Note 3.

notes.text: LING courses at 2000 and above level as well as those labeled as # will be included in the calculation of Major GPA for honours classification.

Students may be required to participate in activities such as field trips and study tours that foster their learning of linguistics. Students are responsible for part of or all costs incurred in relation to these activities.
Students whose first language is not Chinese may take Cantonese and Putonghua as language courses for 3(b).

A Linguistics Major student who pursues a second Major in Chinese Language and Literature can be exempted from taking CHLL3162 and 4161 by taking LING1002 and 3108 respectively. Units earned can be counted towards both Major Programmes.
A Linguistics Major student who pursues a second Major in Psychology can be exempted from taking PSYC3430 by taking LING3202. Units earned can be counted towards both Major Programmes.
A Linguistics Major student who pursues a second Major in Translation can be exempted from taking TRAN2610 by taking LING3401. Units earned can be counted towards both Major Programmes.
The course not taken to fulfill requirement 2(a) may be taken as a free elective course.

requirement_schemes.title: Linguistics and Translation Double Major Programme

parts.description: Students are required to complete a minimum of 90 units of courses as follows:

sections.title: Faculty Package
text: LING1000# and any two courses from: ANTH1020, ARTS1009, 1010, BMBL1001[a], CHES1101 or 1102, CHLL1900 or 1902 or 1903, CURE1000 or 1400, 1110, ENGE1000, FAAS1900, HIST1000 or 1700 or 1701, JASP1090, MUSC1000, PHIL1110, THEO1000

subsections.title: Four courses chosen from the 3 Areas below, with at least one course from each area
Language and Culture, and Linguistic Applications

text: Students are required to complete 27 units of elective courses from the following lists of courses, including at least one course from each of Electives Cluster A and Electives Cluster B

sections.title: Research Component/ Capstone Course/ Final Year Project

notes.text: LING courses at 2000 and above level as well as those labeled as # will be included in the calculation of Major GPA for honours classification.

Students may be required to participate in activities such as field trips and study tours that foster their learning of linguistics. Students are responsible for part of or all costs incurred in relation to these activities.

Students are encouraged to learn a modern language or take courses in a discipline relevant to a translation area in which the student would like to specialize after graduation using their free electives.

Subject to approval by the Major Programmes concerned, students may opt out of the Double Major Programme and register for the 1st Major Programme only. The decision to opt out is irrevocable. Students who have opted out are required to complete and fulfill all graduation requirements by following the study scheme of the 1st Major Programme as a single major. Students should be aware that such decision may result in a delay in graduation because the requirements of the single major study scheme differ from those of the Double Major Programme.
If the course is not taken to fulfill requirement 1, it may be taken as an elective course for fulfillment of requirement 3(a)(iii).
The course not taken to fulfill requirement 2(a) may be taken as a free elective course.
Inclusion of this course in the calculation of Major GPA is subject to approval.
